QUOTE: The failure becomes an **empty `std::vector<int32_t>`**. The same empty vector also means "empty input" and "vocab is null", which the code handles silently with no log.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states that a failed tokenization returns an empty vector, the same value returned when the vocab is null (no tokenizer wired), and that the interface can't distinguish them.
